title: One worker's sitting, as a durable envelope
intro: A session is one execution episode in one worktree. It claims no paths and gates nothing; it exists so that the records an episode wrote can be read back together, selected by the session stamp each ledger line carries.

scenarios.title: Opening an episode
scenarios.explain: The identity fields are computed from git. The worker is recorded only because it was supplied; an unrecorded worker stays unrecorded rather than guessed.

scenarios.title: Opening a second one here
scenarios.explain: One open session per worktree. Replacing the first would orphan every record it stamped, so the second is refused and told what to do first.

scenarios.title: Closing into an envelope
scenarios.explain: The closed record names the tasks, checkpoints, handovers, decisions and questions of the episode and copies none of them. The path printed is the record, under the layer's tracked sessions section: a closed episode is a shared object (ADR 0014).

scenarios.title: Closing when nothing is open
scenarios.explain: Absence is reported as a missing artifact, exit 12, and never as a silent success.

scenarios.title: The episode's working context, composed now

stdout_contains: not stored and is not a snapshot

scenarios.explain: `session context` composes the live working context on every read: the episode's own record, git now against git at the open, and the episode's ledger lines. Nothing in it is a stored document somebody had to write.

scenarios.title: Where the episode's opening snapshot is
scenarios.explain: `start` freezes what the context builder resolved into the local working-context store, and `--path` prints where that snapshot is rather than its contents.
